subject: FintechCo — Post-demo SLO checklist & decision criteria
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechco.com>, Samir Gupta <samir.g@finpay.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo — Post-demo SLO checklist & decision criteria

Hi Alex / Samir,

Thanks again for taking the demo today — appreciate the candid conversation about performance constraints for your customer-facing risk scoring service. Per our call, I put together a concise SLO checklist and proposed decision criteria so your team can validate Redwood against the requirements that matter for go/no-go. Attaching the checklist and a short performance notes PDF.

Quick summary of what we heard and what we want to validate with a short test run: 
- Latency: target P95 < 120 ms for 512-token inference (interactive scoring path).
- Throughput: sustained 200 req/s for the batched scoring API (average payload ~300 tokens).
- Concurrency: steady 50 concurrent live sessions with bursts to 200 for traffic spikes (burst allowance important for peak windows).
- Streaming: required for the live chat use case — target time-to-first-token < 50 ms; incremental token latency < 20 ms.
- Availability/Failover: automated fallback to lower-capacity model variant with <1% request error on overload.

Proposed next-step mutual action plan (MAP):
1) You confirm the decision criteria above (or call out adjustments).
2) Redwood runs a focused load/streaming test against a short harness (we’ll provide scenario + test harness).
3) Joint review of results + recommended kernel/quantization config.
4) If results meet your decision criteria, we’ll scope Dedicated capacity / pilot pricing.

Can you confirm the latency/throughput numbers above match FintechCo’s expectations or flag where they differ? If so we’ll schedule the test the week of Jun 14 and share a short runbook.

Thanks,
Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachments: fintechco_slo_checklist.xlsx, redwood_performance_notes.pdf
From: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo — Post-demo SLO checklist & decision criteria

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and the checklist. A few clarifications from our side after syncing with the infra team: 
- Latency: P95 target of 120 ms is our ideal for interactive scoring, but acceptable threshold is P95 < 150 ms for 512 tokens. P99 we expect < 250 ms.
- Throughput: sustained 200 req/s is correct for the batch scoring window; important caveat is payload varies — we may see spikes to 350 req/s for short bursts during end-of-day recon.
- Concurrency: steady 50 is accurate; however we should plan tests for concurrency = 100 and burst to 300 to be safe (our traffic can double during promotions).
- Streaming: absolutely required. Our internal SLA needs time-to-first-token <= 40 ms for chat-like flows. Incremental token latency target is <= 25 ms.

Also: for the pilot we’ll want the load tests to run from our us-west region to match production pathing and to validate egress costs with our cloud setup. We can provide a small dataset and a service account for the test harness.

If Redwood can meet P95 120 ms in your baseline config that’s a strong signal — but to be explicit our decision criteria for pilot approval will be: P95 <= 150 ms (512 tokens), sustained 200 req/s with tested bursts up to 300 req/s, streaming first-token <= 40 ms.

Available next week for a 30-min sync Thu 10–11 PT or Fri 2–4 PT to finalize the MAP.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Platform Engineering, FintechCo
alex.j@fintechco.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.j@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Jun 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo — Post-demo SLO checklist & decision criteria

Alex / Marissa,

Thanks — good notes. Quick responses and proposed test plan from our side: 
- We’ll aim to baseline with the Redwood-verified model variant and our recommended quantization profile that preserves P95 latency. If P95 is within 120–150 ms we’ll surface the exact kernel/quantization choices in the results report.
- For throughput and burst testing we’ll run two phases: a sustained 20-minute run at 200 req/s and a burst phase with 5x short bursts (30–60s) up to 300 req/s to validate graceful degradation/fallback.
- Streaming tests: we’ll measure time-to-first-token and incremental token latencies using your provided harness. We can instrument first-byte latencies with our tracing and provide a token-level breakdown.
- Region: tests will be executed from us-west to mirror your production footprint.

We’ll need the following from FintechCo to get started:
- Short test dataset + sample payload shapes (small files fine)
- Service account or endpoint details for the harness (read-only test creds)
- Preferred test window for the week of Jun 14 (we can do Tues/Wed morning PT)

I’ll attach the short runbook and a draft test schedule (see attached). Proposed owners: Aditya (Redwood) for test execution, Alex (FintechCo) to validate traffic shape, Marissa to coordinate post-test review.

Aditya
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_test_runbook.md

Date: Sat, 5 Jun 2027 14:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo — Post-demo SLO checklist & decision criteria

Alex — thanks for the clear decision criteria — I’ve summarized below and converted into MAP items so we’re aligned before the test run. Please reply to confirm or edit.

Decision criteria (FintechCo for pilot approval):
- P95 latency <= 150 ms (512 tokens); P99 < 250 ms.
- Sustained throughput 200 req/s with validated bursts up to 300 req/s.
- Streaming: time-to-first-token <= 40 ms; incremental token latency <= 25 ms.
- Test executed from us-west with FintechCo-provided harness.

Mutual action plan (MAP) — next steps: 
1) FintechCo: share test dataset + harness creds by Jun 9.
2) Redwood: schedule test window for Jun 14 or Jun 15 (Aditya to execute).
3) Redwood: deliver results report with config recommendations and token-level latency breakdown within 48 hours of test completion.
4) Joint review: 30–45 minute review call to decide Pilot scope within 3 business days of results.

I’ll create the HubSpot opportunity note and add the MAP there (link below). Can we lock Thu 10:30 PT on Jun 10 for a final pre-test sync? If that works I’ll send an invite.

Thanks — looking forward to the test run.

Marissa
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
